claim_1.claim: Gene array analysis of whole blood from 15 YF17D-vaccinated individuals in the Montreal cohort at days 0, 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60 after vaccination showed that gene expression modulation peaked at days 3 and 7 after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The peak of modulation of gene expression, as shown by heat map representation (Fig. 1 a) and principal component analysis (Fig. 1 b), primarily occurred at days 3 and 7 after vaccination, whereas a limited number of significant genes were modulated in response to vaccination at day 10 after vaccination or beyond.

Figure 1. Vaccination with YF17D induces early gene modulation. Global view of gene modulation in total blood cells after YF17D vaccination, as analyzed by gene array on the Montreal cohort (n = 9–15, depending on the time point). Heat map representation (a) and PCA (b) using the significantly modulated genes, in at least one comparison versus day 0.

comparison.finding: gene expression modulation at day 3 relative to baseline
gene expression modulation at day 7 relative to baseline
a limited number of significant genes were modulated at day 10 relative to baseline
a limited number of significant genes were modulated at day 14 relative to baseline
a limited number of significant genes were modulated at day 28 relative to baseline
a limited number of significant genes were modulated at day 60 relative to baseline

ranking.metric: gene expression modulation relative to baseline
ranking.finding: gene expression modulation peaked at day 3 and also primarily occurred at day 7 after vaccination

claim_2.claim: Gene array analysis of whole blood from 15 YF17D-vaccinated individuals in the Montreal cohort at days 0, 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60 after vaccination showed that TLR-associated genes (TLR7, MYD88, and IRF7) and IFN-induced genes (IFI27, IFI30, G1P2, G1P3, and OAS1-3) were up-regulated early after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Some Toll-like receptor (TLR)-associated genes (TLR7, MYD88, and IRF7) were also up-regulated, leading to the activation of the IFN pathway, as monitored by the induction of several IFN-induced genes (IFI27, IFI30, G1P2, G1P3, and OAS1-3; Fig. 3 a and Supplemental document 1).

Figure 3. YF17D vaccination stimulates multiple arms of the innate and adaptive immunity. (a–e) Heat map representation of significantly modulated genes, P values listed with each gene indicate the largest (least significant) P value among the significant fold changes. n = 9–15, depending on the time point. The listed genes fall under different functional categories: IFN-induced and TLR-associated genes (a); complement-associated genes (b); macrophage-associated genes (c); NK cell-associated genes (d); and B cell-associated genes (e).

claim_8.claim: Gene array analysis of whole blood from volunteers in the Montreal cohort at day 3 after vaccination showed that inflammasome-associated genes caspase-1 and caspase-5 were up-regulated compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Our gene array results showed that two components of the inflammasome, caspase-1 and -5, were up-regulated at the mRNA level in the Montreal cohort, 3 d after vaccination with YF17D (Fig. 5 a).

Figure 5. YF17D induces expression of genes associated with IL-1β and activates the inflammasome. (a) Heat maps showing the up-regulation of genes encoding inflammasome components and the modulation of other, IL-1β-associated genes.

comparison.finding: inflammasome-associated genes caspase-1 and caspase-5 were up-regulated at day 3 compared to baseline

claim_9.claim: ELISA analysis of supernatants from monocyte-derived DCs incubated with live, UV-inactivated, or heat-inactivated YF17D showed that live or UV-inactivated YF17D induced markedly increased IL-1β secretion compared to DCs incubated in medium alone.

sources.quote: The results show that DCs incubated with live or UV-inactivated YF17D showed a marked increased IL-1β secretion (up to ninefold, compared with DCs incubated in medium alone), whereas heat-inactivated YF17D only triggered a modest secretion of the proinflammatory cytokine (Fig. 5 b and Fig. S4, available at http://www.jem.org/cgi/content/full/jem.20082292/DC1).

Figure 5. YF17D induces expression of genes associated with IL-1β and activates the inflammasome. (b) IL-1β production by monocyte-derived DCs incubated with live (YF), UV-inactivated (UV), or heat-inactivated (HI) YF17D, as determined by ELISA.

comparison.finding: live YF17D induced markedly increased IL-1β secretion compared to DCs incubated in medium alone
UV-inactivated YF17D induced markedly increased IL-1β secretion compared to DCs incubated in medium alone
heat-inactivated YF17D triggered only modest IL-1β secretion compared to DCs incubated in medium alone

claim_11.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 6 volunteers at days 0, 3, 7, 10, 14, and 28 after YF17D vaccination showed that frequencies of Ki67+ CD4+CD8− cells and Ki67+ CD4−CD8+ cells increased within the first 14 days after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: An increase in frequencies of Ki67+ cells in the CD4+CD8− (2.3-fold increase; P = 0.0049) and the CD4−CD8+ (4.7-fold increase; P = 0.0157) populations occurred within the first 14 d after YF17D vaccination, and then decreased to insignificant levels.

claim_12.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 6 volunteers at days 0, 3, 7, 10, 14, and 28 after YF17D vaccination showed that frequencies of Ki67+ NK cells and Ki67+ non-T cell PBMCs containing monocytes and B cells increased within the first 7 days after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The Ki67+ NK cell population (CD3−CD8Dim; 1.6-fold; P = 0.0474) and non–T cell PBMCs containing monocytes and B cells (CD3−CD4−CD8−; 1.9-fold; P = 0.009) also increased in frequency within the first 7 d and reached insignificant levels thereafter.

claim_16.claim: Cytometric bead assay analysis of PBMC supernatants from YF17D-vaccinated volunteers stimulated with YF17D-derived peptide pools at day 60 after vaccination showed that both Th1 and Th2 cytokine secretion profiles were induced in most volunteers compared to unstimulated conditions.

sources.quote: In most volunteers (12 out of 15), both Th1 and Th2 cytokine secretion profiles were induced by YF17D peptide pools.

Figure 6. YF17D induces a mixed Th1/Th2 response. (a) Day 60 PBMCs were stimulated with the 22 peptide pools and assayed by CFSE labeling for their proliferative response. Bar graphs show data for six selected volunteers, and the dataset for all the volunteers can be found in Fig. S6 (c and d). At 24 h of culture, supernatants were analyzed by CBA to determine the Th1/Th2 cytokine secretion profile in response to each pool.

claim_17.claim: Polychromatic flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from vaccinated volunteers at day 28 after vaccination showed that YF17D-specific CD4+CD154+ T cells expressed IL-2 alone, IFN-γ alone, or both IL-2 and IFN-γ after peptide stimulation compared to unstimulated cells.

sources.quote: As illustrated in Fig. 7 a, 35.2% of CD4+CD154+ cells expressed IL-2 alone, 8.6% expressed IFN-γ alone, and 29.5% expressed both IL-2 and IFN-γ.

Figure 7. YF17D vaccination induces specific CD4+ T cells of mixed T helper phenotype. (a) PBMCs from YF17D-vaccinated volunteers (day 28 after vaccination) were stimulated with a group of three immunostimulatory YF17D-derived peptides pools, and then stained with antibodies against CD4 (surface) and CD154, IL-2, and IFN-g (intracellular).

claim_18.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from four volunteers at day 365 after vaccination showed that both Th1 and Th2 central memory T cells could be detected after stimulation with YF17D peptide pools compared to background stimulated-only samples.

sources.quote: However, both Th1 and Th2 central memory T cells could be detected in all four volunteers tested.

Figure 7. YF17D vaccination induces specific CD4+ T cells of mixed T helper phenotype. (b) FACS analysis of PBMCs from day 365 after vaccination. Cells from four volunteers were stimulated (S) for with immunostimulatory YF17D peptide pools, and then restimulated (RS) or not with the same peptide pools before staining. The data were analyzed according to the gating strategy shown in Fig. S7, and are expressed as the percentage of central memory CD4+ T cells (CD45RA−CCR7+) that express the marker for recent activation CD154, and that are either Th1 or Th2 in the RS samples, over background (S).

claim_19.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of DC/T cell co-cultures from YF-naive individuals showed that DCs pulsed with live or UV-inactivated YF17D primed a strong antigen-specific response of naive T cells compared to no-antigen conditions.

sources.quote: As shown in Fig. 8 a, DCs pulsed with YF17D virus (live or UV-inactivated) primed a strong antigen-specific response of naive T cells, with up to 4% cells expressing CD154 and IFN-γ in response to live or UV-inactivated YF17D.

Figure 8. YF17D elicits robust and diverse primary T helper cell responses in DC/T cell co-cultures. (a and b) Purified T helper cells were mixed with DCs that had been incubated with live or UV-inactivated YF17D. After 14 d, the cells were harvested and evaluated by flow cytometry for cytokine and CD154 expression after a short restimulation with autologous DCs targets that had been left untouched, pulsed with killed YF17D, or infected with live YF17D.

claim_20.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of DC/T cell co-cultures from YF-naive individuals showed that YF17D-pulsed DCs stimulated high numbers of antigen-specific Th2 cells expressing IL-5 and IL-13 upon restimulation with live or inactivated virus compared to no-antigen conditions.

sources.quote: Similarly, YF17D-pulsed DCs stimulated high numbers of antigen-specific Th2 cells expressing IL-5 and IL-13, upon restimulation with live or inactivated virus (Fig. 8 b).

Figure 8. YF17D elicits robust and diverse primary T helper cell responses in DC/T cell co-cultures. (a and b) Purified T helper cells were mixed with DCs that had been incubated with live or UV-inactivated YF17D. After 14 d, the cells were harvested and evaluated by flow cytometry for cytokine and CD154 expression after a short restimulation with autologous DCs targets that had been left untouched, pulsed with killed YF17D, or infected with live YF17D.

claim_21.claim: Multiplex cytokine analysis of supernatants from MIMIC DC/T cell co-cultures showed that when YF17D was used as pulse and recall antigen, the cells produced high levels of IL-2, IFN-γ, IL-13, and IL-5, but not IL-10, compared to co-cultures with no recall antigen.

sources.quote: When YF17D was used as pulse and recall antigen, the cells produced high levels of all the cytokines measured except IL-10, compared with co-cultures with no recall antigen.

Figure 8. YF17D elicits robust and diverse primary T helper cell responses in DC/T cell co-cultures. (c) Alternatively, the culture supernatants were harvested and evaluated by a multiplex cytokine analysis.

claim_22.claim: Microarray analysis of cells from MIMIC co-cultures harvested at day 7 versus day 0 showed that eight transcriptional nodes of downstream target genes, including ETS2, STAT1, IRF1, IRF7, IRF8, GATA1, LMO2, and JUN, were consistently identified after YF17D stimulation compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Gene modulation in response to the antigen (day 7 vs. 0) was assessed by microarray analysis. In total, eight nodes of transcriptional regulation of downstream target genes were consistently identified; ETS2, STAT1, IRF1, IRF7, IRF8, GATA1, LMO2, and JUN (Fig. 9).

Figure 9. Consensus transcriptional network of genes differentially expressed on day 7 as compared with day 0. Network representation of inferred transcription factors and predicted target genes that are consistently modulated in at least two out of three datasets, with the third dataset not being contradictory.

comparison.finding: Eight transcriptional nodes of downstream target genes, including ETS2, STAT1, IRF1, IRF7, IRF8, GATA1, LMO2, and JUN, were consistently identified on day 7 after YF17D stimulation relative to day 0 baseline.
